items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: he told me that Art Tatum was going to be there. So I had to wait around for that.

ctx.x: I used to go around with Oscar Pettiford, every place he went he would always — if he didn’t have a lady with him — he would always say, “Come on let’s go hang.” And we’d go in the after hour joints during the day and in the evening you know and play. And I’d sit and watch him play and all like that. And the worst basses in the world. You know you

go in an after hour joint and you know, they don’t have good basses there. Or you go into a club, some obscure club you know, and he would just wink at me. He’d go like this. I’m going to show him. But he was teasing me you know. And he’d make this guy’s bass sound just like, like it was a Stradivarius or something. I remember once, I don’t want to hold you, but once I went into an after hours joint and he told me that Art Tatum was going to be there. So I had to wait around for that. Art came in and he sat down…
You’ve got to negotiate with the instrument.
